data.name: Rajih
data.gender_notes: Rajih is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: One who is vindicated, just and fair. Derived from the Arabic root 'R-J-H' meaning to be upright and just. The name Rajih carries the meaning “Vindicated, just” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Rajih usually hope their child will grow to embody vindicated, just and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A person who is guided by Allah's justice and mercy.
data.etymology: Rajih belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Vindicated, just.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rajih total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: In Islamic culture, the name Rajih signifies someone who stands up for what is right, just and fair. It implies a person with strong values and unwavering position, when it comes to defending their beliefs, principles and morals. It is a name for those seeking to live within the moral framework and be recognized symbolically as upright and just individuals.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, the name Rajih signifies a person who is striving towards righteousness and justice, both within their inner self and in their relationship with God. It is a reminder of the importance of moral conduct and individual character development, as well as an inspiration to be a beacon of truth and fairness in the world. This name also reflects the divinely ordained qualities of patience, perseverance, and fairness, all of which are essential for living a virtuous and fulfilling life according to Islamic teachings.
data.spiritual_symbolism: The meaning "Vindicated, just" symbolizes One who is vindicated, just and fair. Derived from the Arabic root 'R-J-H' meaning to be upright and just..
